response.explanation: The postInit duplicate check is sound. Grant IDs are unique provider IDs, so grantsToShortcuts has one entry per grant plus UNKNOWN. grantsByShortcuts has one entry per distinct shortcut plus UNKNOWN. Equal sizes therefore require all shortcuts to be distinct, and a shortcut that collides with the UNKNOWN value also shrinks the map and is caught. A duplicate cannot hide behind equal map sizes. The lazy-refresh paths only run for keys missing from the maps, and both maps are ConcurrentHashMap. A concurrent refresh writes the same key/value pairs, so the maps cannot end up inconsistent. A late-deployed grant with a colliding shortcut, or a disabled-feature grant that cannot be decoded, is speculative. The snapshot gives no evidence for either.

response.consequence: expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken no longer verify that the token ID encodes the right grant type. Regressions in token ID encoding would pass the integration tests unnoticed.
response.explanation: The token ID format is `<sessionType 2><tokenType 2><grant 2>:<uuid>`, for example `trltcc:1234`. The grant shortcut sits at indices 4..6. The matcher does two things wrong. (1) It uses `substring(3, 5)`, which for `trltcc` is `tc`, not `cc`. (2) It returns false when the substring EQUALS the expected shortcut. This is the reverse of the intended check. With the intended grant at the right position, the matcher would reject every correct token ID. Because of the wrong offset, it almost always passes for any grant. A wrong grant (e.g. `ac` instead of `dg`) is accepted, and the test is not meaningful. A grant-shortcut mismatch is never detected. If the offset is later fixed without fixing the inversion, every correct token would be rejected. A token ID shorter than 5 chars would also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.

replacement.original:
// Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char and is 2-chars long
                if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
replacement.text:
// Grant type shortcut starts at the 5th char (index 4) and is 2-chars long
                if (items[0].length() != 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;

A caller can pass rawTokenId = null, for example getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(ctx, null), and the constructor accepts it. The error message says rawTokenId is validated, but it is not.

hypotheses.evidence_needed: A set of grant factories, including a custom one, that has duplicate shortcuts but equal map sizes. A race or inconsistency between the two maps. A disabled-feature grant whose tokens cannot be decoded after a feature toggle.
hypotheses.failure_mode: The shortcut maps are populated only once in postInit and never rebuilt consistently. The lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut write to the two maps non-atomically, and neither path checks for shortcut collisions. A grant type whose shortcut collides with another's, or with the reserved 'na', silently overwrites an entry. A token ID could then decode to the wrong grant type. Also, the duplicate check compares only map sizes, so it can pass when two grants have the same shortcut and the same-size inversion happens to hide the collision. The disabled EnvironmentDependent grant factories (CIBA, device, token exchange, pre-authorized code) are also absent from getProviderFactoriesStream.
hypotheses.investigation_rationale: Check the postInit duplicate detection and the lazy-refresh logic. Look at the shortcuts across all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations ('rt' for the refresh grant and 'rt' for TokenType are in separate namespaces, but check 'ac', 'cc', 'ro', 'pg', 'te', 'pc', 'ci', 'dg'). Also check for third-party grant factories.
hypotheses.priority_rationale: The token ID is used for event and introspection decisions. A wrong grant type mapping or an unexpected IllegalStateException at startup would affect token issuance.

hypotheses.evidence_needed: Callers that decode a token ID without catching IllegalArgumentException. Grant paths that call createClientAccessToken with no GRANT_TYPE attribute. Tests/events that expect an unprefixed UUID.
hypotheses.failure_mode: initToken now always encodes the token ID as '<session><token><grant>:<uuid>' and relies on Constants.GRANT_TYPE being set in the ClientSessionContext. Grant flows that don't set it (the authorization code, the CIBA and device flows, any other createClientAccessToken callers) fall back to 'na'. Refresh sets 'refresh_token'. getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException on any ID that contains ':' but is not a 6-char prefix. Consumers that parse the 'jti' (introspection, revocation, logout, existing tokens with other formats) may throw a 500 instead of a clean rejection. userSession.getPersistenceState and userSession.isOffline are used to compute the session type; the offline refresh and offline-session-created-from-online paths may be mislabelled.
hypotheses.investigation_rationale: Trace all callers of getTokenContextFromTokenId and all consumers of AccessToken.getId. Check that every grant sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE before token creation, and what happens when a 'jti' contains ':' in a custom or federated token.
hypotheses.priority_rationale: The change affects every token issued. A thrown exception on a malformed ID or a mislabelled session type changes security-relevant behaviour and events.

hypotheses.failure_mode: The new abstract method getShortcut() on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks any external or custom grant factory compiled against the old SPI. They fail with AbstractMethodError when the encoder calls getShortcut() during postInit or lazily. Even without that, a custom grant with a missing or colliding shortcut makes startup fail with IllegalStateException. The new Context.getGrantType() reads formParams.getFirst(grant_type) in the constructor. If grant flows replace form params later (setFormParams), createTokenResponse can embed a stale or null grant type; a null value would make a later AccessTokenContext creation fail or give 'na'.
